title_en: Sorangi (a hymn in the Sorang strain)
translation:
Here begins Shri Sorangi ||16||

1. Jire — I entreat Saraswat Swami and beg one favour of him: with simple, artless bhakti (devotion) I shall sing of you, who are the king of a million universes.
[refrain: Sorangia]

2. In the sorang strain let us meditate on Shri Hari; let us worship Kanhan (Krishna) of Gokul. Harji, Hari, Parbrahm who is the supreme Parbrahm — great and weighty are your names.
[refrain: Sorangia]

3. Jire — the ocean of worldly existence is hard to cross, exceedingly deep and without limit; take the name of Ram as your vessel and cross over to the far shore.
[refrain: Sorangia]

4. Jire — he who breaks and fashions a million universes: how can he be contained in a little basket? To whom shall I offer flowers and leaves, when the fourteen worlds lie inside his mouth?
[refrain: Sorangia]

5. Jire — knowing the wisdom of the Self, I delight in [unclear] his qualities. He pervades a million universes: that is the absolute Brahm, beyond all speech.

6. Jire — serve him who is tender towards his devotees; why then keep up your wailing? Serve him who removes the anguish of the womb and every sorrow — hold this conviction firmly in your mind.

7. Jire — when King Ambarish was being harassed by a snare, he remembered lord Murari; and to keep the word of both the sage and the king, he took incarnation ten times over.

8. Jire — he took the form of a fish, dark of hue, and playfully churned through the ocean; in that same instant he seized the demon Panchajan in his hand and brought back the Vedas with ease.

9. Jire — Narayan took the form of the tortoise and bore Mount Mandar upon his back; gods and demons together made one company, and made the serpent their churning-rope.

10. Janardan took the form of a woman and held the pot of nectar in his hand; deceiving the demons, Hari gave it to the gods to drink, and every purpose of the gods was fulfilled.

11. Jire — in the boar form he held the earth on the tip of his tusk and set her back in her place; Hari removed the affliction of the gods, and the bones of the demons were broken.

12. Jire — in the man-lion form he tore him open with his claws and slew the demon king; bursting the pillar apart Hari came forth, and showed his grace to his devotee.

13. Jire — as Vaman he made Bali a dweller in the netherworld and removed Indra's affliction; there the Lord assumed his universal form and set his foot upon Bali's back.

14. Jire — Parashuram broke the power of the kshatriya lords and raised up the brahmin folk; he requited the wrong done to the great sage and removed his father's grief.

15. Jire — the sage's curse upon Dasharath was worked out, and all the matters were accomplished; the king performed a sacrifice and asked for sons, and there Shri Ram descended.

16. Jire — he took the incarnation of Ramchandra and did the work of the earth; for Sita's sake he slew Ravan and gave the kingdom to Vibhishan.

17. The eternal one, together with Lakshman and Sita, took the kingship of Ayodhya; the supreme Lord seated in the flower-chariot — and all the tasks were accomplished.

18. Jire — in the form of Ram he pervades everything; whatever you look upon, know it as him. See how he removes the anguish of the womb and every sorrow; mighty is his command.

19. Jire — by the Vedas you are known, and yet the Vedas do not reach your far shore; pervading all in the form of Ram, you are the support of devoted folk.

20. Jire — he was born in the house of Nand the cowherd, and made Gokul his abode; to graze the cows over the twelve forests and the hill, Govind and Ram took birth.

21. Jire — earrings glitter at his ears, and on his breast a garland of gunja berries; a peacock-feather crown is set upon his head — boundless is Kanhad's beauty.

22. Jire — little Kanha the cowherd goes out to the forest to graze the cows; he eats and, eating, feeds others — he who bears up Brahma and all the gods.

23. Jire — he climbed the branch of the kadamb tree and plunged into the water of the Yamuna; Hari danced upon the hood and bridled Kali (Kaliya) the serpent.

24. Jire — his garment a yellow silk, his wrap a cloth of nine colours; Hari came riding the serpent for a saddle — that great Yadav hero.

25. Jire — in Gokul he sounded the horn, in Vrindavan he played the flute; he broke the bonds of his mother and father, and Kanha slew Kans.

26. Jire — the infinite one passed eleven years, keeping company with Ram (Balram); the teacher had him study his lessons, and he grew up in great delight.

27. Jire — for the sake of the marriage he drove Shishupal off, and wedded eight queens; and further he married women in many various ways, and had sixty lakh sons.

28. Jire — Hari came to Shonitpur and won the battle against Har-Swami (Shiv); he cut off the arms of Banasur, and Okha obtained Aniruddh.

29. Jire — Nar and Narayan came mounted on the chariot, and at that hour he showed his universal form; Hari removed the affliction of the Pandavs, destroying eighteen akshauhini armies.

30. In the Buddha form Hari pondered in meditation and took up the path of yoga; in the Kalki form, to put down the wicked, he took undying weapons in his hands.

31. Jire — let us meditate on him in all ten incarnations, and in the twenty-four of the Bhagavat; serve him who removes the anguish of the womb and every sorrow — the supreme Purush, the Lord of the world.

32. Jire — let us meditate on such a Lord of the earth, who is beyond reckoning and beyond all possibility; hard to reach even for the mind of the lord of yogis — you who are Brahma and all the rest.

33. Jire — let us sing the virtues of Govind, and meditate besides in many ways; if the Lord of compassion shows his grace, then knowledge of the Self awakens.

34. Jire — the four-armed one in the courtyard, robed in yellow silk, with the crown shining upon his head; he sports there together with Lakshmi, and the minds of the Vaishnavs are enchanted.

35. Jire — let us meditate on the imageless King, and know him both as form and as formless; follow the path of the Vedas, and bring devotion and feeling into your mind.

36. Jire — with leaves of tulsi worship the enemy of Putana; cast off delusion, envy and pride, and come to understanding through knowledge of the Self.

37. Jire — let us serve Hari together with Lakshmi, and serve his divine play and sport; he fulfils the fruit the heart desires — that King, Shri Avinash, the imperishable one.

Thus ends Sorangi, complete ||16||
The third rest of the five-day parayan (recitation) is complete.
